statement: The oldest confidently-dated Homo erectus/ergaster fossil is KNM-ER 2598 (an occipital/cranial fragment), East Turkana, Kenya, dated to approximately 1.88-1.9 million years ago, stratigraphically below the KBS Tuff; this dating was reaffirmed with new associated postcrania in 2021 after decades of uncertainty because the original specimen was a surface find.

sources.citation: Hammond, A.S., Royer, D.F., Fox, N.S., et al. "New hominin remains and revised context from the earliest Homo erectus locality in East Turkana, Kenya." Nature Communications 12: 1939.
sources.author: Hammond et al.

adversarial_counter: KNM-ER 3733, a more complete and famous cranium often cited in popular sources as illustrating the species’ first appearance, is actually dated to roughly 1.6-1.78 million years ago — several hundred thousand years younger than KNM-ER 2598 — and should not be used as the earliest-appearance anchor.
